messages:
Tess: dropping this week's Nimbus health snapshot. Short take: WoW tokens +23%, QoQ +47%. Spend +14% WoW. p95 latency up ~45ms. Errors ~5.4% (mostly 429, a few 503s during bursts).
Vik: thanks. Any odd signal in routes or keys? 503s worry me more than the 429s.
Tess: embeddings route jumped unexpectedly ": /v1/embeddings" now ~20% of tokens (used to be ~9%). Main token pressure still /v1/generate (~58%). Two keys dominate: nimbus-main (69%) and nimbus-embed (19%). 503s correlate with short multi-second spikes and GPU slot saturation on a few nodes.
cloud-bot: [ALERT] acct_nimbus - 5m 429 rate = 5.0% (threshold 3.5%). 503 spike detected on serve-node-7. Dashboard: https://dd.example.com/d/nimbus/health
Hannah: I pulled node metrics  serve-node-7 and serve-node-9 show higher GPU mem pressure and occasional OOM restarts during the embedding bursts. Looks like their embed workload has different seq-len distribution that increases memory usage.
Rafael: did they change client-side behavior? QoQ growth +47% normally means product change.
Tess: product notes show they shipped an "instant-index" feature that calls embeddings more often. Also some customers started sending longer docs which increases per-call token counts.
Vik: mitigation ideas: 1) short-term: enable soft throttling on key nimbus-embed during peak windows and route heavy embedding batches to a dedicated pool; 2) medium-term: suggest moving long-doc embeddings to an async batch job (we can host a batch path); 3) recommend client-side concurrency cap and batching.
Hannah: I'll prepare telemetry slices. Sample BigQuery used: 
```sql
SELECT api_key, route, SUM(tokens) tokens, COUNT(*) calls, APPROX_QUANTILES(latency_ms,100)[OFFSET(95)] p95_ms
FROM `redwood.telemetry.events`
WHERE account_id='acct_nimbus' AND event_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
GROUP BY api_key, route
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
Hannah: top rows: nimbus-main /v1/generate = 58% tokens (p95 430ms), nimbus-embed /v1/embeddings = 20% tokens (p95 520ms), rerank ~12%.
Rafael: that p95 for embeddings is high. Probable cause: long seq lengths + GPU mem fragmentation. Also the occasional 503s point to node OOMs. Can ops temporarily bump the pool size or move embedding traffic to lower-util nodes?
Vik: ops already increased autoscale upper bound yesterday from 6->8, but some nodes are heterogeneous and dont have enough memory. Short-term actionable: 1) create a dedicated embed pool with larger-memory instances, 2) apply a soft throttle policy for nimbus-embed during 10:00-12:00 UTC, 3) enforce batching window.
Tess: sample SDK guidance to send to their engineers (both JS + Python) 
```js
// JS: reduce concurrency + favor batching
const client = new RedwoodClient({concurrency:3, batchWindowMs:40});
client.enablePrefixCache('/v1/generate');
```
```py
# Python: for embeddings, prefer async batch endpoint
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(concurrency=2, batch_window_ms=100)
# if using long docs, call /v1/embeddings/batch_async
```
Hannah: I'll attach per-hour heatmaps and a node-level OOM trace to ticket RED-4321.
Rafael: cost scenarios for AE: Option A) provision a dedicated embed pool (higher base cost, reduces p95 and 503s) -> estimated +12% monthly; Option B) keep current infra + enforce client batching + soft throttle -> estimated -8% monthly but requires client changes. I'll crunch exact numbers once Hannah posts telemetry.
Vik: also note renewal risk: moderate. If we don't show reduced errors or cost improvements before renewal review, AE wants to offer a consumption-based discount. Rafael, please draft the renewal brief.
Tess: scheduling: propose a 30m enablement + infra sync focused on embeddings and batching. Options: Thu 14:00 UTC or Fri 09:00 UTC. Who can join?
Hannah: I can do Thu 14:00 UTC and will share traces and heatmaps.
Rafael: Thu 14:00 UTC works for me to present cost models. Vik: available as well.
Tess: ok I'll propose Thu 14:00 UTC to the Nimbus team and include AE + infra eng. Action items: Hannah -> attach telemetry + node traces to RED-4321; Vik -> draft soft-throttle config + autoscale tweak PR; Rafael -> cost scenarios + renewal brief; Tess -> outreach + schedule. Re-open if error rate >6% before Thu. :rocket:
